title: Part
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to zero and the translation vector also set to zero. Proceed to draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face, which consists of a single loop made up of four lines. The first line begins at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and extends horizontally to (0.0365, 0.0). The second line starts from this point and moves vertically to (0.0365, 0.75). The third line continues from here, moving horizontally back to (0.0, 0.75), and the fourth line completes the loop by returning to the origin. After completing the sketch, apply a scale factor of 0.75 to reduce its size proportionally. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional object by rotating it with the Euler angles set to zero and translating it with the translation vector set to zero. Finally, extrude the sketch 0.0156 units along the normal direction to create a solid body. This results in a cylindrical object with a slightly wider base and a narrower top, featuring smooth surfaces and rounded edges. The final dimensions of the part are a length of 0.036458333333333336 units, a width of 0.75 units, and a height of 0.015624999999999998 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0365, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0365, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.75) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a cylinder
r = r.extrude(0.0156)

# Scale the sketch (if needed)
# Note: The sketch scale is applied before extrusion, but in this case, it's 0.75 which is the same as the width.
# So, we don't need to scale the sketch explicitly in this example.

# The final model is represented as 'r'
